final_md.old: Every note here is one sinusoid under one decay. The Synthesis Lab adds such sinusoids together on purpose; what the ribbon drew for you as a sum is where that begins.
final_md.new: Every note here is one sinusoid under one decay. Sky Stairs next asks what a sampled curve needs before it can become a place for a body. The beat display then separates two ongoing motions from their sum. In the Synthesis Lab, we will add such sinusoids together on purpose; what the ribbon drew for you as a sum is where that begins.

registry.old: Metal bars that ring—each bar's length determines its pitch, shorter bars vibrate faster. Strike them to hear wavelength become sound, to feel the relationship between physical size and frequency.
registry.new: Strike-triggered synthesized tones: chosen note frequencies set each bar’s visible length. Each bar plays one decaying sine voice; striking it again restarts that voice. The table stand displays their sampled source-audio sum before spatial attenuation.

registry.old: Builds a helical staircase around a central column, modulating tread radius with a sine wave.
registry.new: A helix of separate treads with sine-modulated radius and uniform rise. Optional membranes, rails or posts expose what must be added to sampled positions; colliders exist, while a complete ascent and headset comfort require separate testing.

registry.old: Walkable path generated by trig functions
registry.new: A retained secondary installation with two finite rows of collidable steps whose heights follow sine and cosine over a shared descent. The shipped scene circulates existing steps in opposite directions; it does not generate an endless path from the visitor’s position.

registry.old: Interactive demonstration of additive wave synthesis — layer sine waves of different frequencies and amplitudes to build complex waveforms. Visualizes Fourier's fundamental insight that any shape can be constructed from simple oscillations.
registry.new: A visual additive-synthesis instrument with five nonnegative, phase-locked sine coefficients. Its sliders form finite harmonic sums; nearby recipe names use a coefficient tolerance. The optional bench provides HOLD, H1 ALONE, BASELINE and a component-sum readout.
